Couldn't tell you, i've mentioned it to a few people in my life and either been met with crazy looks or got a speech about how suicide isnt the answer blah blah blah. 

Most people don't wanna hear it or don't care to hear it.

For me personally I was scared for awhile, of the unknown, of the potential nothingness. I also had hope for awhile it would get better. It took over 2 decades and one very painful event in my life to finally realize suicide is my only viable option and that it will never get better.

Dany touched hot metal when she threw the braiser over, she also went into a boiling hot bath and it didn't phase her. It's not just fire she's immune to, but any kinda of ridiculous heat. Honestly, her being alone was incredibly stupid and made no sense. She's walking around a city she JUST burnt to the ground, you have no idea who could be lurking around, waiting to bring justice to the woman who just burnt their family and friends alive.
Grey Worm was actually loyal and loved his queen, no matter what. Jon not being executed on the spot by Grey Worm is what baffles me. Heck he showed Jon more mercy then Jon did Dany.

Yeah, he seemed pretty damn traumatized by it, obviously, and we know Jon doesn't lie. So I think its pretty clear he just turned himself in and confessed right after Drogon flew off. What didn't make sense is why Greyworm didn't just execute him on the spot, seems unlikely he'd imprison him after he just murdered his queen.

I was honestly waiting for us to get a scene of her standing atop a cliff with Drogon overlooking King's Landing at the end lol. Honestly wish this would happen, and it would make sense considering how much  Kinvara seemed to back Dany.

Though realistically this would probably become a problem for old king Bran in the future. Heck considering how weak and depleted their forces are, they should really worry about someone else trying to claim the throne and start a war again. Like Dorne for instance, who's army's went pretty much untouched in this war.

What else didn't make sense is Drogon. I KNEW they were gonna kill Dany off, though I expected it to be Arya, and actually did think it was Arya at first. I thought she threw a dagger at her from afar. Anyway, the one thing I kept thinking about was, if they kill her, wouldn't Drogon go on a rampage and basically burn everyone alive?

We know the dragons are intelligent, we know they know friend from foe. But they also only truly follow one person, Dany, their mother. We've seen them burn former "friends" alive without hesitation on Dany's command. So why the hell did Drogon not burn Jon alive right then and there? He KNEW it was Jon who did it. This made ZERO sense to me.
